board.empty: The roster is empty. Put a project in roster.json and run murscope again.
board.promise: Reads only the projects you listed - `init` with no path names the directories it looked in to propose them. Writes nothing into them. Makes no network call.
board.promise.network: Reads only the projects you listed - `init` with no path names the directories it looked in to propose them. Writes nothing into them. This install carries the [ai] extra, so it can make a network call: nothing runs unless config.toml names it, and nothing is sent until you have been shown what leaves and have agreed to it. `murscope selftest` names every module here that could open a socket.
board.tagline: What is moving, what stalled, what is stuck on you.
board.title: murscope
hint.activity: The activity clock is off. Switched on, it reads file times inside the projects you listed and adds a second, weaker line under the commit clock.
hint.ai: An API key would add a written daily note over these rows. The board is complete without one.
hint.github: A GitHub token would add review state: draft pull requests, and issues assigned to you. It is not required and nothing here waits for it.
hint.title: Not switched on
method.inferred: An inference is never shown as a declaration. It carries a badge, a dashed rule, and the evidence that produced it.
method.overlap: This project's directory is inside MURSCOPE_HOME. Nothing is written to it, but the write guard can no longer be the thing that proves so - its boundary and this directory overlap.
method.state: A state is declared when a ledger line says so, curated when you wrote it, and otherwise inferred from what the project has in hand. What is in hand is stated whichever way the clock reads; these thresholds change the wording only: uncommitted {uncommitted}d, unpushed {unpushed}d, WIP commit {wip}d, stash {stash}d. A clean tree reads as moving within {moving}d and as quiet after it. A declaration older than {stale}d is marked stale.
method.title: How this board decides
method.trend: Trend reads the commits in the {window}-day window. None at all reads dormant; none in the last {recent} days reads stalled; fewer than {floor} in the window says the sample is too small rather than guessing. Past those three, the last {recent} days are compared against the {prior} before, per day: at or above {up}% of the earlier rate it reads accelerating, at or below {down}%, slowing. Where every commit is recent there is no earlier rate to compare against, and it says that instead of calling it acceleration.
stat.owed_blind: no ledger line could be matched to you: either no owner names are configured, or a line names somebody these names do not cover. Check blockers.owner_aliases
stat.owed_partial: and {count} more name somebody these owner names do not cover - the number below is what could be matched, not the total
state.inferred.stash.aged: interrupted a long time ago: {entries} stash entr{ies}, oldest {days} days
state.inferred.touched: touched {days} days ago, no version history to read
state.inferred.uncommitted.aged: set aside: {files} file{s} uncommitted, {days} days quiet
state.inferred.unpushed.aged: {commits} commit{s} finished but never sent, sitting {days} days
state.no_source.text: No readable ledger, and no weak signal to fall back on.
state.none.text: Read and computed: nothing worth flagging.
state.stale: the ledger line is more than {days} days old
